text:
alisha: Quick sync — I prototyped a cheap dedupe-attribution flow for edge-collected traces. Want feedback on the heuristics before we put anything in the gateway.

trent: sharing the gist? how aggressive is 'cheap'?

alisha: gist: we fingerprint spans by (trace_id, span_name, service_fingerprint) then soft-ttl for 30s at the edge, drop exact duplicates, and attach a dedupe_hint attribute so central pipeline can reconcile. pseudo: ```
fingerprint = sha1(trace_id + '|' + span.name + '|' + svc_fp)
if cache.has(fingerprint) and now - cache.get_ts(fingerprint) < 30s:
  emit(span with dedupe_hint=true)  # cheap drop at edge
else:
  cache.put(fingerprint, now)
  emit(span)
```

katie: neat. what's svc_fp? are we assuming deterministic service id?

alisha: svc_fp is a small stable fingerprint based on service name + version + binary hash (same as our edge provenance header). deterministic for a given deploy.

sam: two quick tradeoffs: 1) dropping at edge skews cost attribution vs central billing — if we drop, the central metering might miss tokens. 2) dedupe_hint requires central merge logic; if teams expect 1:1 ingestion events they could be surprised.

matt: agree. Also, dedupe window matters for retries. 30s seems reasonable for user-facing paths but maybe too long for background pipelines. Can we make window adaptive by route?

alisha: plan was route-configurable: short for internal metrics (5s), longer for API frontdoor (30s), and per-tenant override. Defaults backed by a safe-mode where edge never drops, just marks.

trent: can we avoid missing billing? Maybe we always emit a tiny "cost_token" heartbeat for dropped spans so billing pipeline still sees an entry but central storage avoids full payload duplication.

alisha: I considered that. Heartbeat idea: emit a compact envelope with fingerprint + billing_key + size_estimate. Central billing uses that for tallying while full payload still dropped. Upside: much cheaper bandwidth. Downside: added complexity + cardinality on billing topic.

sam: cardinality is the main risk. We already see spikes when services emit many unique fingerprints. If heartbeat includes fingerprint, that becomes high-cardinality. But if heartbeat contains only billing_key + approximate_token_count we lose precise dedupe accounting.

katie: what about hashing fingerprint -> small bucket id (e.g., mod 1024) in heartbeat? reduces cardinality but introduces collision bias into cost attribution. We could estimate correction factors offline.

matt: collision bias might be acceptable if we surface uncertainty ranges in billing UI. Teams would get a 99% confidence estimate instead of exact counts. For enterprise customers wanting exact billing, we can disable edge-drop and route everything through central.

alisha: suggested policies:
- default: edge soft-drop + heartbeat(bucket_id, billing_key, approx_tokens)
- enterprise: no-drop, full-replay to central
- debug: mark-only (no drop) for a tenant while debugging regressions

trent: operational checklist? what do we need in console/observability to make this safe?

alisha: good Q. Minimum:
- dashboard: dropped_count by route/tenant, and heartbeat-volume by bucket
- anomaly alert: sudden drop volume changes > 3x per 1h window
- audit log: per-tenant policy changes (who changed)
- backfill path: enable central reingest for a tenant for a past window if accounting mismatch is reported

sam: also add a simulation tool: replay 24h of edge data through the dedupe logic offline to estimate billing delta. Make that required before enabling for a tenant.

matt: latency measurement: ensure heartbeat path is low-overhead and doesn't affect p95. We should have a microbenchmark on gateway CPU/mem with 10k rps.

katie: question on central merge: if we drop full spans at edge and rely on heartbeat for billing, how do we present traces to users? Concern: trace UI may show missing spans for some requests.

alisha: UX plan: trace UI will indicate when spans were deduped at edge (banner) and attempt to reconstruct using sampled central spans + cached edges for a short window. For full fidelity, user can toggle "disable dedupe" for a trace capture session.

trent: sounds reasonable. action items?

alisha: I'll open an RFC PR that includes: heuristic pseudocode, heartbeat schema (fields: bucket_id, billing_tenant, approx_tokens, fingerprint_meta_count), simulation harness, and console metrics.

sam: assign owners: alisha (prototype + RFC), katie (billing/metrics impact review), matt (gateway perf tests), trent (central merge + backfill), and SRE for alerting runbook.

ingest-bot: Reminder: created ticket INF-7392 to track dedupe-heartbeat integration.

katie: +1. I'll run a small historical estimate this week and post numbers. If bucketing looks biased, we'll tweak bucket count.

matt: thanks — let's have a short follow-up sync after RFC is up. :thumbsup:

alisha: thanks everyone — RFC will be up by EOD tomorrow.
